scope: Three peer-reviewed primary field studies for previously undocumented topic sections. Facts are historical and site-specific.
policy: No species absence, national status, local occurrence certainty, modelled presence, or universal life history inferred.

records.label: Mount Sinaka incubation record
records.text: A Philippine Eagle pair studied at Mount Sinaka incubated one egg for 58 days; the female accounted for 74% of observed incubation time.
records.sourceLocation: Abstract; Mount Sinaka pair observed July 1999–January 2000
records.studyScope: One documented central Mindanao nesting pair; 58 days and female attendance are observations, not an invariant across all Philippine Eagles.

records.label: Mount Sinaka prey delivered to nest
records.text: The studied pair's 17 recorded prey items included four vertebrate taxa; civets and Philippine colugos comprised most identified prey in that nest sample.
records.sourceLocation: Abstract; diet of the observed Mount Sinaka pair
records.studyScope: 17 prey items from one nest, July 1999–January 2000; not a population-wide prey percentage or habitat occurrence estimate.

records.label: Northeast Mindanao field microhabitats
records.text: The 2016 northeast Mindanao surveys encountered this frog at agricultural edges beside second-growth vegetation, tree nurseries and lowland forest riparian sites.
records.sourceLocation: Species account: Leptobrachium lumadorum, habitat observations
records.studyScope: Survey encounters in northeast Mindanao; some disturbed-site detections do not establish equal survival in all disturbed habitats.

records.label: Mountain encounter elevations
records.text: Sanguila and colleagues reported specimens on the mountains Magdiwata, Hilong-hilong, Balatukan and Lumot at elevations reaching 1,500 m.
records.sourceLocation: Species account: Leptobrachium lumadorum, elevational field records
records.studyScope: Maximum elevation mentioned for sampled northeast Mindanao mountains, not a national elevation tolerance or confirmation of absence elsewhere.

records.label: Trees used for feeding in field study
records.text: A study of six Philippine colugos monitored feeding among trees at its study area, where the researchers enumerated 76 available tree species.
records.sourceLocation: Abstract; observed trees and study vegetation sampling
records.studyScope: Six observed Philippine colugos at one study area in 1986–1987; feeding substrate evidence, not a national habitat suitability classification.

records.label: Documented tree use during foraging
records.text: Six observed colugos fed on 35 of 76 available tree species, representing at least 12 plant families, in the 1986–1987 study.
records.studyScope: Six colugos and 76 inventoried tree species; the observed 35 species are not a complete diet list for the Philippines.

records.label: Repeated short nocturnal feeding visits
records.text: The tracked colugos made many short feeding visits during the night and used several tree species within individual nights.
records.studyScope: Six animals observed in 1986–1987; no assertion that all individuals share the same nightly activity schedule.
